page: Microsoft Azure D96ds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv6 server family. It is built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and runs on an x86_64 architecture. The server features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor with 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of memory, providing a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The hardware configuration includes 5669 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the D96ds_v6 demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities and high memory throughput. The server achieved a top-tier PassMark CPU score of 86698.13 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 21967.0. Multi-core stress-ng performance is rated as strong at 79846.28, while single-core performance on stress-ng is average at 1949.09. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, reaching 6196.47 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 257.11 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. The processor's support for Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) is reflected in strong extended instructions testing and top-tier image processing benchmarks.

With its high-density dedicated compute resources and substantial local storage, the D96ds_v6 offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring high parallel processing power without the overhead of dedicated GPU hardware. The server is suited for database operations, as evidenced by a strong PassMark database score of 32248.97 and 107.53 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. It also excels at static web serving, achieving a top-tier throughput of 116.39 GB/sec. Other appropriate workloads include software compilation, text processing, and CPU-based LLM inference, where it processes 7B model prompts at 282.63 tokens per second.
